messages:
sophia.procure: Heads up 026-05 pilot quote from MetricLoop looks off. They applied a pilot credit but also charged a "platform enablement" fee we explicitly excluded. Can finance/billing weigh in?

mike.finance: paste snippet? need to see numbers to advise.

olga.sales: their rep said credits are "invoice reductions only" and cannot be used to meet committed tiers. that's not what we asked.

sophia.procure: snippet they sent:
```
Invoice #2026-ML-77
- Ingest (GB): 2,400 @ $0.012 = $28.80
- Event processing (10k): 180 @ $5.50 = $990.00
- Platform enablement: $1,800.00
- Pilot credit: -$1,500.00
Net due: $1,318.80
```
They also attached terms saying: "Pilot credits are non-transferable and shall not reduce minimum commit thresholds."

drew.billing: operationally we can accept invoice reduction, but not the exclusion from tiering. Tax/VAT impacts differ if credits convert to prepayment. Need an example credit memo and how they'd apply conversion on year-1 invoice.

mike.finance: from a P&L/accounting perspective, two safe options: A) credits are treated as prepayment and reduce committed liability (preferred), or B) credits remain invoice discounts only (we'll require clearer econ modelling). If we want A, legal must sign amendment language: "Pilot credits, upon execution of an amendment within 30 days of invoice, shall be converted to prepayments applicable to the first 12 months of committed services and reduce committed fees dollar-for-dollar."

olga.sales: propose negotiation asks: 1) allow conversion of up to 70% of pilot credits to year-1 commit if amendment executed within 30 days; 2) waive/credit the enablement fee for the pilot or convert it into credits; 3) vendor to provide SOC2 Type II or attestation within 45 days for any ingest of device identifiers.

sophia.procure: i'll request that language and ask for sample invoice showing conversion and a single credit memo. Also asking vendor to confirm whether ingest is measured compressed or uncompressed (we saw mismatches previously).

vendorbot: MetricLoop uploaded revised terms v1.3: https://metricloop.example.com/terms/2026-05-10 (doc)

drew.billing: add that any conversion must include an auditable CSV export of pilot usage and a single credit memo ID so we can reconcile. Also require clause preventing double-counting of credits across invoices.

mike.finance: let's add an audit right for 12 months post-conversion to verify credits vs. usage logs. If vendor resists 70% we can accept 50% + SLA credits.

olga.sales: i'll push rep. if they push back on SOC2 timeline, offer a reduced-scope pilot (non-PII only) until compliance is provided.

sophia.procure: draft message to vendor: "We will pay the pilot invoice on the condition you (1) issue a corrected invoice removing enablement fee or convert it to credits, (2) agree to amendment language converting up to 70% of pilot credits to year-1 prepayment upon signed amendment within 30 days, (3) provide sample credit memo + usage CSV, and (4) deliver SOC2 attestation within 45 days or accept narrowed pilot scope." sending now.

vendorbot: MetricLoop replied: "Rep is reviewing. Can we do 50% conversion and 60-day amendment window?"

mike.finance: counter: 60-day window exposes us to recognition/tax complexity. insist on 30 days. Offer 55% conversion if they insist on 60 days.

drew.billing: also ask for explicit invoice example showing tax/VAT treatment post-conversion. Can't finalize AP entries without that.

sophia.procure: agreed. i'll push 55% + 60-day compromise only if they provide immediate corrected invoice removing enablement fee. We'll hold non-disputed portion per our dispute policy. Tagging @mike.finance @drew.billing for final sign-off once vendor sends corrected invoice and sample memo.

mike.finance: ok to proceed with that path. will review corrected invoice on receipt.

drew.billing: will prep AP hold memo and chartfield instructions. thanks.
